exact_statement: For every even k>=4, r>=2k, and C>=6, let F be the canonical quadratic bent k-bit function and its zero-vertex point flip, activated by r fresh point controls and selected by a fair physical selector. On the complete selector-controls-adjacent-data-pairs tree with irrelevant inputs skipped and constant leaves, the minimal nonnegative reserve Q*_v=[D_v-C Inf_v+average Q*_children]_+ vanishes at every control node and even point-edited paired-data entry. Odd edited data states have Q*<=2. For physical minority mu(g)=min(P[g=-1],P[g=+1]), every node obeys Q*_v<=4mu(g_v)log2(1/mu(g_v)); at the root Q*=[D_selector-C 2^{-(r+k)}]_+<4*2^{-k}mu(F)log2(1/mu(F))<=mu(F)log2(1/mu(F))/4 and Q*<=2^{1-k}I(F). At r=2k and fixed finite C, Q*/I(F) is asymptotic to (2/5)2^{-k}. In particular the C=6 reserve certificate gives H(F)<=(6+2^{1-k})I(F)<=49I(F)/8. Pointwise credit domination is not a local drift assertion for the rarity function, which remains false on these selector roots for fixed coefficients. Extension: For every even t>=2, every single vertex sign flip of a quadratic bent t-core, with any coordinate character phase, has zero complete increasing-pair-order entry reserve at every C>=6. For every even k>=4, T_k=b_k with sign flips at zero and e_1+e_3 has zero complete paired-entry reserve at C>=6. At its first query both children retain one edit; the expensive character-mate child has zero reserve and the other child reserve is at most two bits. If the clean core and T_k are activated by r>=2k point controls and selected by a fair bit, then all control entry reserves vanish, Q_root=[D_selector-2C*2^(-r-k)]_+, Q_root<8*2^-k*psi(mu) and Q_root<=4*2^-k*I_root; at C=6, H<=(6+4*2^-k)I<=25I/4. Its exact initial influence is 2^-r[k/2+r(1-2^(-k/2)+2^(1-k))+(2k-2)2^-k]. Original all-node rarity and asymptotic conclusions are retained only for the original one-zero-edit selector family; they are not asserted for the new phase or two-edit families.
